_about: What each destination creates for a PostgreSQL NUMERIC column declared with no precision and no scale.

No fixed-width type holds every value such a column can hold, so a PostgreSQL destination gets plain NUMERIC and every other destination stores the exact value as text (product decision, 2026-09-28). A destination table that already exists keeps its column type.

Batch: PostgreSQL discovery reports such a column with the bare type "numeric". A bare "decimal" keeps meaning a fixed-width decimal, because MySQL and Oracle report constrained columns that way. shared/mcp-connectors/tests/test_unconstrained_numeric_golden.py checks canonical_to_ddl against batch_ddl and fixed_decimal.

CDC: Debezium sends such a column as io.debezium.data.VariableScaleDecimal. The kafka-sink-worker's unconstrained_numeric_golden_test.go checks mapConnectFieldToDDLType against cdc_ddl. An empty string means the worker names no type, so the destination connector creates its text type.
